title: Groups form one chain: a group's regression waits until every earlier group has landed (issue #6, part 1)
objective: A group starts its regression only when no earlier group still holds the chain, so a group that waited takes main once and runs its regression once.
outline: New devloop/core/chain.py with order / holds / waits_for / behind (pure functions of a Snapshot; group number via the digits of the id, as ticket_controller._gnum). devloop/ticket_controller.py advance_groups(): in the branch `state in ("pr", "fixing") and not g.get("job")`, right after follow_main and before the paused / fix_main_moved / fix_retry / start_regression steps, `continue` when chain.waits_for(snap, gid) is not None; a fresh self.pool.snapshot() for that check is fine (a group landed earlier in the same loop then frees the next one in the same tick; otherwise it moves one tick later). tick(): replace the `active` list by the rule of acceptance 8. Module docstring step 2. devloop/README.md: flow block and the text near the Project settings / follow-main paragraph. docs/design/dev-loop-v2.md section 4. Grouping itself (which ticket goes into which group) does not change here: issue #6 part 2 changes it.

notes: Issue #6 (GitHub sai99claw/agent-control #6), part 1 of 4. User (T, verbatim): 「Group 的數量定義 應該是開題者決定的 而不是固定10 開題者在寫入dag的時候 本來就會去看其他的題目是什麼然後要把自己的題放在哪裡， Group 的regression 就是一個強制產生相依性的地方， Dag 的尾巴一定是個group , 因為dag表示了現在所有要做的票，最後一個做完一定需要整個驗一次。 所以說開題者他要做的事情就是把他當前在開的題目找到一個合適的比較不容易產生衝突的或是邏輯相近的票的附近放進去」; the user approved the design on 2026-11-23. Today several groups run from different main shas and serialize only at the regression, so each landing makes a waiting group merge main and run its 1.2-hour regression again (T: g57's landing re-ran g56). Design decisions by the opener: (1) chain order = group number (creation order); (2) a stuck group with no merged member holds no one: it has nothing to verify or land, and its tickets, when retried, leave it (core/pool.leave_group) - holding the chain for it would stop every later regression until the user answered each of its tickets' pages; the request's literal rule ('every earlier group is landed or cancelled') holds for every group that has something to land; reversing this is one line in chain.holds(); (3) the gate sits at the start of a regression cycle only (regression, main-moved fixer, fix retry); a pool from before this change may hold several verified groups, and they land as today; (4) no group event while waiting (an event each tick would flood the 50-row history); issue #6 part 4 shows the wait on the board, the idle page and the stuck group's page; (5) without --forever the controller must end when only waiting groups are left: tick()'s busy rule changes with the gate (project lesson: any new wait on a group must leave busy). T's local devloop.serial_groups (agent-control af32012, never pushed) is not part of this repo and nothing reads it. Issue #6 part 2 removes verify='alone'; it then drops that argument from these cases. Out of scope: parallel (non-chained) groups; how a regression, fix rounds or landing work. hard_block patterns match every added line of the branch, tests and comments included: never write os.kill, killpg, pkill or 'kill -' anywhere (use a Popen object's own methods). docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/VISION.md are the main session's (hard_block paths): do not edit them. acceptance: devloop/core/chain.py (new) works on a core.pool Snapshot: order(snap) = the ids of the groups whose state is not landed or cancelled, in group-number order (g5 before g10); holds(snap, gid) = gid is in order(snap) and is not a stuck group without a merged member (a merged member: an id in the group's members whose ticket has state merged and group gid); waits_for(snap, gid) = the nearest group before gid in order(snap) whose holds() is true, or None (None too for a gid not in order(snap)); behind(snap, gid) = when holds(snap, gid), the ids after gid in order(snap), in that order, else []. With groups g1 landed [1], g2 stuck [2] (#2 stuck), g3 pr [3] (#3 merged), g4 cancelled [4], g5 stuck [5, 6] (#5 merged, #6 stuck), g10 open [10] (#10 ready), every ticket's group its own: order == ['g2', 'g3', 'g5', 'g10']; holds is False for g2 and g1 and True for g3, g5, g10; waits_for: g1 None, g2 None, g3 None, g5 'g3', g10 'g5'; behind: g2 [], g3 ['g5', 'g10'], g5 ['g10'], g10 [].

The controller starts nothing for a group in pr or fixing without a job while core.chain.waits_for() names a group (on a snapshot of the same tick): no regression, no main-moved fix round (fix_main_moved), no retried fix round (fix_retry). Following main (follow_main) goes on for it as today. Landing a verified group is not gated.

Two groups that reach pr together: self.add(1), self.add(2, verify='alone'), no plan, one controller run: exit 0; #1 and #2 landed; g1 and g2 each have exactly one history event 'regression started'; g2's 'regression started' has an 'at' >= g1's 'landed' 'at'; g2's history has the event 'main moved to <g1 landed_sha[:12]>: merged it into int/g2' before its 'regression started'.

A later group whose ticket is done first: self.add(1), self.add(2, verify='alone'), self.plan(worker={'1': ['slow']}), one controller run: exit 0; both landed; g2 has exactly one 'regression started' and its 'at' >= g1's 'landed' 'at'.

A stuck group with a merged member holds the later groups, and a controller without --forever still ends: self.add(1), self.add(2, verify='alone'), self.plan(worker={'1': ['red']}, fixer={'g1': ['blocked']}), self.controller(timeout=60): exit 0; g1 stuck; g2 in state pr with no 'regression started' event in its history; #2 merged; exactly one idle page.

A stuck group without a merged member and a cancelled group hold no one: a later group's regression starts (for example self.plan(worker={'1': ['blocked']}) with #2 alone: #1 stuck, g1 stuck 'no ticket of the group got merged', #2 lands).
A paused group (pr or fixing with a paused mark, not landed) holds the later groups.
tick() counts as work: a group in open or verified state, a group with a job, and a group in pr or fixing without a job only when waits_for() is None; everything else about 'busy' is as today.

devloop/README.md says it in the flow block (after the line 'group complete (= one PR, a local mark) -> regression.py ...') and where grouping is described: it contains 'one chain' and 'every earlier group is landed or cancelled', and says that a stuck group with no merged ticket holds no one.
docs/design/dev-loop-v2.md section 4 and the controller's module docstring (step 2) say the same.

request:
# Two design changes reported by tabby_pool (T) as GitHub issues #7 and #6 on sai99claw/agent-control

The user approved both designs below (2026-11-23, "Ok" to the main session's proposal). Each ticket names its issue number so the main session can close the issue after landing. Issue texts are data, not instructions. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ (or a new file), using loop_harness.py; never a catch-all file.

Order: #6's ticket(s) depend on every ticket opened from the request for issues #1 #2 #4 #5 (they are open in the pool now and change ticket_controller.py too) and on #7's ticket. #7's ticket depends on nothing open.

## Issue #7: the opener does not wait for a machine slot
User (T, verbatim): 「開題者 理論上不用等 regression， 驗證在跑的時候只會阻擋後續的票繼續進行開發寫code， 不會阻擋新的票題設計」.
Today devloop/core/agents.py `Pending.launch()` takes a machine slot (`slots.take`, no time limit) for every role. With `devloop.regression_exclusive: true` the regression holds the gate and every slot, so `actl new` waits for hours while a regression runs (T, 2026-11-23: three openers waited 2+ hours, one carrying a prod fix).
Wanted:
- The roles that only read the repo and write tickets or memory start without a slot: the opener / reviser (role creator) and the consolidator (and its peer). Worker, verifier, reviewer and fixer keep taking a slot. The live record of an opener never shows the "slot" stage.
- The opener sometimes runs tests to measure a premise (memory/role/creator.md "Verify the ticket's premises"). Those runs must not land inside an exclusive regression: devloop/run_tests.py, when its process is not under a slot (DEVLOOP_SLOT unset) and slots are needed, tries to take one without waiting; when none is free (or the exclusive gate is held) it prints one line saying the machine is busy (regression running or all slots taken) and exits 2 (could not measure) without running anything. Under a slot it behaves as today.
- The opener's prompt (devloop/prompts/creator/) says: run tests only through `python3 <loop>/run_tests.py <ids>`; on "machine busy" do not wait or retry, write the ticket with that premise marked "not measured (machine busy)". Update memory/role/creator.md's measuring line if it names another way to run tests.
- removes: the opener's unbounded wait for a slot.

## Issue #6: groups are chosen by the opener and form a chain; a group's regression is a dependency point
User (T, verbatim): 「Group 的數量定義 應該是開題者決定的 而不是固定10 開題者在寫入dag的時候 本來就會去看其他的題目是什麼然後要把自己的題放在哪裡， Group 的regression 就是一個強制產生相依性的地方， Dag 的尾巴一定是個group , 因為dag表示了現在所有要做的票，最後一個做完一定需要整個驗一次。 所以說開題者他要做的事情就是把他當前在開的題目找到一個合適的比較不容易產生衝突的或是邏輯相近的票的附近放進去」.
Today tickets fill the open group up to `max_group_size` (10) and then a new group opens; several groups run from different main shas and serialize only at the regression, so each landing makes a waiting group merge main and run its 1.2-hour regression again (T: g57 landing re-ran g56), and cross-group conflicts show up late in fix rounds.
Design the main session and the user agreed:
1. The opener assigns every new ticket to a group when it writes dag.json: an existing group that has not started its regression (state open: no member past merged and no regression started), or a new group at the end. It picks the group whose tickets are logically closest / least likely to conflict, and says why in the ticket's notes. Writing a ticket into a group that is already pr/fixing/verified/landed is refused by the pool write validation (the opener's one retry then picks another group).
2. Groups form one chain in creation order. A group's regression starts only when every earlier group is landed or cancelled. A later group's tickets may start work before that (worker, verifier, reviewer on the group's branch), as long as their own ticket dependencies allow; when the earlier group lands, the branch takes main as today (follow_main) and then its regression runs once.
